# 2025 Spending Dashboard Overview

A 3-chart dashboard will show your first-half 2025 spending from three angles: **trend**, **mix**, and **change**. Use the same color for each category across all charts so the story is easy to follow.

## Recommended Dashboard Layout

| Chart | Best Chart Type | What It Shows | Main Insight to Reveal |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Line chart | Monthly spending trend by category | Which categories are rising, flat, or seasonal |
| 2 | Stacked bar chart or donut chart | Category mix across Jan–Jun | Which categories dominate total spend |
| 3 | Month-over-month change chart | MoM increases/decreases by category | Where the biggest jumps and dips happen |

## Chart-by-Chart Plan

### 1) Spending Trends by Category
**Chart type:** Multi-line chart
**X-axis:** Months (2025-01 to 2025-06)
**Y-axis:** USD spent
**Series:** Rent, Groceries, Transport, Dining Out, Entertainment

**What it should reveal**
- **Rent** is stable, with a step-up from **$1,800 to $1,850** in April.
- **Groceries** show the clearest upward trend, ending at the highest level in June.
- **Transport** rises gradually with minor variation.
- **Dining Out** fluctuates more than essentials, with a noticeable lift in March and June.
- **Entertainment** stays relatively low and steady.

**Best use**
- Spot trend direction and compare category growth over time.
- Highlight whether essentials or discretionary spending are driving changes.

### 2) Category Mix Across the 6 Months
**Chart type:** Stacked bar chart by month, or donut chart for total Jan–Jun mix
**If using stacked bars:** one bar per month, stacked by category
**If using donut:** total spending aggregated across all 6 months by category

**What it should reveal**
- **Rent** is by far the largest share of total spending.
- **Groceries** are the second-largest recurring expense and a meaningful share of variable spend.
- **Dining Out** and **Transport** form a mid-tier spending band.
- **Entertainment** is the smallest category.

**Best use**
- Show where most of the budget goes.
- Make it easy to see fixed vs variable spending concentration.

### 3) Month-over-Month Changes
**Chart type:** Bar chart of MoM deltas, one series per category or a grouped bar chart
**X-axis:** Month transitions (Feb vs Jan, Mar vs Feb, etc.)
**Y-axis:** Change in USD
**Measure:** Current month minus previous month

**What it should reveal**
- The largest positive changes likely come from **Groceries** and **Dining Out** in select months.
- **Rent** shows a single structural increase in April, then remains flat.
- **Transport** changes are modest, suggesting relatively controlled commuting costs.
- **Entertainment** has small swings, useful for spotting discretionary spikes.

**Best use**
- Identify which categories caused budget pressure in a given month.
- Separate one-time jumps from ongoing growth.

## Insight Targets for the Dashboard

- **Trend insight:** Groceries appear to be the fastest-rising recurring category.
- **Mix insight:** Rent dominates the budget, so even small rent changes materially affect totals.
- **Change insight:** Dining Out is the most volatile discretionary category and likely the easiest lever for short-term savings.
